language_specific.usage: The speaker formally tells the audience that they came from Tokyo to the place where they are addressing them.

common.sentence: 皆様、本日は私が司会をいたします。
common.note: 皆様（みなさま） is a formal way to address everyone; 本日（ほんじつ） means today; 司会（しかい） means chairing an event.

language_specific.usage: The speaker formally tells the audience that they will chair the event.

common.sentence: 皆様、次に私が説明いたします。
common.note: 皆様（みなさま） is a formal way to address everyone; 説明（せつめい）する means to explain.

language_specific.usage: The speaker formally tells the audience that they will explain next.

common.sentence: 皆様、私もそのように考えております。
common.note: 皆様（みなさま） is a formal way to address everyone.

language_specific.usage: The speaker formally tells the audience that they share that view.

common.sentence: 皆様、私は今、京都に住んでおります。
common.note: 皆様（みなさま） is a formal way to address everyone; 京都（きょうと） is Kyoto.

language_specific.usage: The speaker formally tells the listener where they currently live.

common.sentence: はい、私はその話を知っております。

language_specific.usage: The speaker formally confirms to the listener that they know about the matter.

common.sentence: 皆様、準備ができるまでお待ちください。すぐ戻ってまいります。
common.note: 皆様（みなさま） is a formal way to address everyone; 準備（じゅんび） means preparation; 戻る（もどる） means to return.

language_specific.usage: The speaker formally asks the audience to wait and says they will return shortly.

common.sentence: 友達「先に帰るね。」私「うん、気をつけて。」

language_specific.usage: The speaker casually tells a departing friend to take care.

common.sentence: 客「これ、袋に入れてください。」店員「かしこまりました。」

language_specific.usage: The clerk formally acknowledges the customer's request.

common.sentence: 友達「この席、空いてる？」私「うん、どうぞ。」
common.note: 席（せき） means seat; 空いてる is a casual form of 空いている.

language_specific.usage: The speaker invites a friend to take the available seat in a casual exchange.

common.sentence: 客「注文をお願いします。」店員「ご注文を承ります。」
common.note: 注文（ちゅうもん） means order; 承る（うけたまわる） is a humble verb used for accepting a request or order.

language_specific.usage: The clerk formally accepts the customer's order, humbly describing the clerk's own action.

common.sentence: 同僚「この資料、今日中に見られる？」私「了解。」
common.note: 同僚（どうりょう） means coworker; 資料（しりょう） means materials; 今日中（きょうじゅう） means by the end of today.

language_specific.usage: The speaker casually acknowledges a coworker's request to review the materials today.

common.sentence: 私「念のため、資料を確認してください。」同僚「はい。」
common.note: 念（ねん） in 念のため is read ねん; 資料（しりょう） means materials; 確認（かくにん） means checking.

language_specific.usage: The speaker asks a coworker politely to check the materials as a precaution.

common.sentence: 友達「明日の映画、行けなくなった。」私「残念！」
common.note: 残念（ざんねん） expresses disappointment.

language_specific.usage: The speaker casually expresses disappointment to a friend who can no longer go.

common.sentence: 客「窓側の席はありますか。」店員「申し訳ありません、満席です。」
common.note: 窓側（まどがわ） means by the window; 満席（まんせき） means fully occupied.

language_specific.target_reading: もうしわけありません
language_specific.usage: The clerk formally apologizes to the customer before explaining that the seats are full.

common.sentence: 友達「この箱、持とうか。」私「助かる、ありがとう。」

language_specific.usage: The speaker casually tells a friend that the offered help is welcome.

common.sentence: 客「水をください。」店員「ただいまお持ちします。」

language_specific.usage: The clerk tells the customer that they will bring water, using a humble expression directed toward the recipient.

common.sentence: 友達「今夜、一緒に食べない？」私「喜んで！」
common.note: 喜んで（よろこんで） expresses willing acceptance.

language_specific.usage: The speaker gladly accepts a friend's invitation to eat together. 喜んで can also be used in polite situations.

common.sentence: 同僚「昼、一緒に食べませんか。」私「ぜひ、ご一緒します。」
common.note: 同僚（どうりょう） means coworker; ご一緒（ごいっしょ）する means to join someone.

language_specific.usage: The speaker eagerly accepts a coworker's polite invitation to lunch.

common.sentence: 友達「手伝おうか。」私「大丈夫、自分でできるよ。」

language_specific.usage: The speaker casually declines a friend's offer of help and says they can manage.

common.sentence: 同僚「今日、飲みに行きませんか。」私「今日はちょっと……。」
common.note: 同僚（どうりょう） means coworker.

language_specific.usage: The speaker leaves the sentence unfinished to decline a coworker's polite invitation indirectly.

common.sentence: 友達「集合は駅前ね。」私「何時だっけ？」
common.note: 集合（しゅうごう） means meeting up; 駅前（えきまえ） means in front of the station. だっけ asks for a reminder of something previously known.

language_specific.usage: The speaker casually asks a friend to remind them of the meeting time.

common.sentence: 客「会計はどこですか。」店員「出口の右側でございます。」
common.note: 会計（かいけい） means payment; 出口（でぐち） means exit; 右側（みぎがわ） means right-hand side.

language_specific.usage: The clerk describes the payment location formally to the customer; the copula shows politeness to the listener.

common.sentence: 友達「先生、もういらしたよ。」私「じゃあ、教室に行こう。」
common.note: 教室（きょうしつ） means classroom.

language_specific.usage: One friend tells another casually that the teacher has arrived, using an honorific verb for the teacher.

common.sentence: 客「田中さんはいますか。」店員「田中は席を外しております。」
common.note: 席（せき）を外す（はずす） means to leave one's desk or place temporarily.

language_specific.target_reading: せきおはずしております
language_specific.usage: The clerk tells the customer formally that Tanaka is away; おります presents the clerk's side politely to the listener.

common.sentence: 同僚「この案はどうですか。」私「検討します。」
common.note: 同僚（どうりょう） means coworker; 案（あん） means proposal; 検討（けんとう） means consideration or evaluation.

language_specific.usage: The speaker politely tells a coworker that they will consider the proposal.

common.sentence: 客「この色はありますか。」店員「確認いたします。」
common.note: 確認（かくにん） means checking.

language_specific.usage: The clerk formally tells the customer that they will check availability.

common.sentence: 客から料理が冷たいとクレームが来た。
common.note: 料理（りょうり） means food or a dish.

language_specific.usage: A customer's complaint concerns cold food. The word is used in ordinary service and workplace contexts.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: く・れ・ー・む; the vowel is long.

common.sentence: 店で買った商品に傷があり、店にクレームを入れた。
common.note: 商品（しょうひん） means product; 傷（きず） means damage or a scratch; 傷があり links “there was damage” to the following action.

language_specific.usage: The speaker lodged a complaint with the shop about damage to a product bought there. This is ordinary consumer vocabulary.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: く・れ・ー・む; the vowel is long.

common.sentence: ホテルの受付は電話で客のクレームを受け付けます。
common.cloze: クレームを受け付けます
common.answer: クレームを受け付けます
common.lemma: クレームを受け付ける
common.note: 受付（うけつけ） means reception; 受け付ける（うけつける） means to accept or receive.

language_specific.target_reading: くれーむおうけつけます
language_specific.usage: The hotel reception accepts customers' complaints by phone. クレーム means a customer complaint in ordinary service contexts; the verb form is polite.
language_specific.pronunciation: The クレーム segment has four morae: く・れ・ー・む; its vowel is long.

common.sentence: 注文した品が違うというクレームに対応した。
common.note: 注文（ちゅうもん）した品（しな） means the item ordered; 対応（たいおう）する means to deal with.

language_specific.usage: The speaker dealt with a customer's complaint about receiving the wrong order. The noun is common in workplace usage.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: く・れ・ー・む; the vowel is long.

common.sentence: あの店は店員のサービスが丁寧だ。
common.note: 丁寧（ていねい） means attentive or polite.

language_specific.usage: The word refers to the attention customers receive from staff. It is neutral in register.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: さ・ー・び・す; the first vowel is long.

common.sentence: このレストランでは食事代にサービス料が加わります。
common.note: 食事代（しょくじだい） means the cost of the meal; 加わる（くわわる） means to be added.

language_specific.usage: The speaker explains that the restaurant adds a service charge to the meal cost. The noun is neutral in register.
language_specific.pronunciation: Six morae: さ・ー・び・す・りょ・う; the /a/ and /o/ vowels are long.

common.sentence: 店員「お茶はサービスです。お代はいりません。」
common.note: お代（おだい） means payment.

language_specific.usage: The clerk tells the customer that the tea is provided free of charge. The word is neutral in register.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: さ・ー・び・す; the first vowel is long.

common.sentence: 店主がサービスで代金を千円安くしてくれた。
common.note: 店主（てんしゅ） means shop owner; 代金（だいきん） means the price.

language_specific.usage: The shop owner gives the customer a discount as a courtesy. The word is neutral in register.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: さ・ー・び・す; the first vowel is long.

common.sentence: 旅行の前日で、妹はテンションが高い。
common.note: 前日（ぜんじつ） means the previous day.

language_specific.usage: The speaker describes their sister as excited ahead of a trip. This sense is casual.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: て・ん・しょ・ん; both nasal morae are pronounced.

common.sentence: 雨で試合が中止になり、みんなテンションが低い。
common.note: 試合（しあい） means match; 中止（ちゅうし） means cancellation.

language_specific.usage: The speaker describes everyone's low spirits after a match is canceled. This sense is casual.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: て・ん・しょ・ん; both nasal morae are pronounced.

common.sentence: 好きな曲が流れて、テンションが上がった。
common.note: 曲（きょく） means a piece of music.

language_specific.usage: The speaker's excitement rises when a favorite song plays. This sense is casual.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: て・ん・しょ・ん; both nasal morae are pronounced.

common.sentence: 楽しみにしていた店が休みで、テンションが下がった。
common.note: 楽しみにする（たのしみにする） means to look forward to.

language_specific.usage: The speaker's spirits fall on finding that a much-anticipated shop is closed. This sense is casual.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: て・ん・しょ・ん; both nasal morae are pronounced.

common.sentence: 兄は背が高くてスマートな体形だ。
common.note: 体形（たいけい） means body shape.

language_specific.usage: The speaker describes their brother's slim build. This appearance sense is neutral in register.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: す・ま・ー・と; the second vowel is long.

common.sentence: その細身の服は、着るとスマートに見える。
common.note: 細身（ほそみ） means slim-fitting.

language_specific.usage: The speaker says the fitted clothes make the wearer look slim. This appearance sense is neutral in register.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: す・ま・ー・と; the second vowel is long.

common.sentence: 彼は皆を待たせないで、スマートに会計を済ませた。
common.note: 会計（かいけい）を済ませる（すませる） means to settle the bill.

language_specific.usage: The speaker describes how smoothly he settled the bill without keeping anyone waiting. This sense is neutral in register.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: す・ま・ー・と; the second vowel is long.

common.sentence: 彼女は相手を傷つけないで、スマートに誘いを断った。
common.note: 相手（あいて） means the other person; 誘い（さそい） means invitation; 断る（ことわる） means to decline. 傷つける（きずつける） means to hurt; here it concerns the other person’s feelings.

language_specific.usage: The speaker describes a tactful refusal that did not hurt the other person. This sense is neutral in register.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: す・ま・ー・と; the second vowel is long.

common.sentence: 去年負けた相手に、決勝でリベンジした。
common.note: 相手（あいて） means opponent; 決勝（けっしょう） means final.

language_specific.usage: The speaker describes beating an opponent in the final after losing to them last year. This sporting sense is informal.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: り・べ・ん・じ; ん is a separate nasal mora.

common.sentence: 前の試合で負けたチームに、次はリベンジしたい。
common.note: 試合（しあい） means match.

language_specific.usage: The speaker hopes to beat a team that won their previous match. This sporting sense is informal.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: り・べ・ん・じ; ん is a separate nasal mora.

common.sentence: 昨日は山頂まで行けなかった。来週リベンジする。
common.note: 山頂（さんちょう） means summit.

language_specific.usage: The speaker plans another attempt to reach the summit after failing yesterday. This sense is informal.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: り・べ・ん・じ; ん is a separate nasal mora.

common.sentence: 一度落ちた試験に、来年リベンジするつもりだ。
common.note: 試験（しけん） means examination; 試験に落ちる means to fail an examination.

language_specific.usage: The speaker intends to retake an examination they previously failed. This sense is informal.
language_specific.pronunciation: Four morae: り・べ・ん・じ; ん is a separate nasal mora.
